q: A motorboat travelling at some speed can cover 24 km upstream and 40 km downstream in 17 hours. At the same speed it can travel 32 km downstream and 12 km upstream in 10 hours. The speed of the stream is:
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let downstream speed = D and upstream speed = U.

We have: 24/U + 40/D = 17 and 12/U + 32/D = 10.

Double the 2nd equation and subtract the 1st: 24/D = 3 ⇒ D = 8 km/h.

Substitute D = 8 in 1st equation: 24/U + 5 = 17 ⇒ U = 2 km/h.

Speed of stream = (D − U) ÷ 2 = (8 − 2) ÷ 2 = 3 km/h.

∴ The correct answer is 3 km/h.

Alternate Method

q: A man can row a distance of 6 km in 1 hour in still water. He can row the same distance in 45 minutes with the current. Find the total time taken by him to row a distance of 16 km with the current and to return to the starting point.
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Downstream speed = Distance ÷ Time = 6 ÷ (45/60) = 8 km/h.

Stream speed = Downstream speed − Still water speed = 8 − 6 = 2 km/h.

Upstream speed = Still water speed − Stream speed = 6 − 2 = 4 km/h.

Total Time = Downstream Time + Upstream Time = (16 ÷ 8) + (16 ÷ 4)

Total Time = 2 + 4 = 6 hours.

∴ The correct answer is 6 hours.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of the man in still water (Vb) = 6 km/h

Distance covered downstream = 6 km

Time taken downstream = 45 minutes = 45 ÷ 60 = 3/4 hours

Distance for final trip = 16 km each way

Formulas Used:

Downstream Speed (Vd) = Vb + Speed of stream (Vₛ)

Upstream Speed (Vᵤ) = Vb − Vₛ

Time = Distance ÷ Speed



Calculations:

⇒ Downstream Speed (Vd) = Distance ÷ Time = 6 ÷ (3/4) = 8 km/h

⇒ We know Vd = Vb + Vₛ

⇒ 8 = 6 + Vₛ ⇒ Vₛ = 2 km/h

⇒ Upstream Speed (Vᵤ) = Vb − Vₛ = 6 − 2 = 4 km/h

⇒ Time taken to row 16 km downstream = 16 ÷ 8 = 2 hours

⇒ Time taken to row 16 km upstream = 16 ÷ 4 = 4 hours

⇒ Total Time = 2 + 4 = 6 hours

∴ The correct answer is 6 hours.

Additional Information

Downstream Speed

When a boat moves in the direction of the stream, the effective speed is the sum of the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the current. Formula: D = Vb + Vₛ

Upstream Speed

When a boat moves against the direction of the stream, the effective speed is the difference between the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the current. Formula: U = Vb − Vₛ

Speed of Boat and Stream from D and U

Speed of boat in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2 | Speed of stream = (D − U) ÷ 2

q: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 200 metres. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is 9 km/h and that of the policeman 10 km/h, how far will the thief have to run before he is overtaken?
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of speeds of Policeman to Thief = 10 : 9

Since the time taken is constant, ratio of distances covered = 10 : 9

Difference in distance ratio = 1 unit = 200 m = 0.2 km

Distance covered by thief = 9 units = 9 × 0.2 = 1.8 km

∴ The correct answer is 1.8 km.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of Policeman = 10 km/h

Speed of Thief = 9 km/h

Initial distance between them = 200 m = 0.2 km



Formula Used:

Relative Speed = Speed of A − Speed of B (in same direction)

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculations:

⇒ Relative speed = 10 − 9 = 1 km/h

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = 0.2 km ÷ 1 km/h = 0.2 h

⇒ Distance covered by thief before being caught = Speed of Thief × Time

⇒ Distance = 9 km/h × 0.2 h = 1.8 km

∴ The correct answer is 1.8 km.

Additional Information

Relative Speed Concept

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their speeds (V₁ − V₂). When moving in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (V₁ + V₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert a speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5 ÷ 18. Conversely, to convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.

Average Speed

When equal distances are covered at different speeds x and y, the average speed for the entire journey is given by (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

q: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 195 metres. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is 22 km/h and that of the policeman is 27 km/h, then how far would the thief have run (in m) before he is overtaken?
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since the time taken by both to meet is the same, the ratio of distances covered is equal to the ratio of their speeds.

Ratio of speeds = Policeman : Thief = 27 : 22

Difference in ratio = 27 − 22 = 5 units

This 5 units represents the initial gap of 195 m ⇒ 1 unit = 195 ÷ 5 = 39 m

Distance covered by the thief = 22 units = 22 × 39 = 858 m

∴ The correct answer is 858 m.

Alternate Method



Given:

Initial distance between Policeman and Thief = 195 m

Speed of Policeman (SP) = 27 km/h

Speed of Thief (ST) = 22 km/h

Formula Used:

Relative Speed (same direction) = S₁ − S₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculations:

⇒ Relative Speed = 27 − 22 = 5 km/h

⇒ Convert Relative Speed into m/s = 5 × (5 ÷ 18) = 25 ÷ 18 m/s

⇒ Time taken by Policeman to overtake = 195 ÷ (25 ÷ 18)

⇒ Time = (195 × 18) ÷ 25 = 140.4 seconds

⇒ Speed of Thief in m/s = 22 × (5 ÷ 18) = 55 ÷ 9 m/s

⇒ Distance covered by the Thief = Speed × Time = (55 ÷ 9) × 140.4

⇒ Distance = 55 × 15.6 = 858 m

∴ The correct answer is 858 m.

Additional Information

Relative Speed Concept

When two bodies move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂). When moving in opposite directions, relative speed is their sum (S₁ + S₂).

Conversion of Units

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by (5 ÷ 18). Conversely, to convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by (18 ÷ 5).

Proportionality of Distance and Speed

If the time taken is constant, the distance traveled by an object is directly proportional to its speed (D₁ ÷ D₂ = S₁ ÷ S₂). This allows solving chase problems instantly using ratio methods.

q: Two trains of lengths 150 m and 250 m run on parallel lines. When they run in the same direction, they take 20 seconds to cross each other and, when they run in the opposite direction, they take 5 seconds to cross each other. What is the speed of the two trains?
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total distance = 150 + 250 = 400 m.

Relative speed in same direction = S₁ − S₂ = 400 ÷ 20 = 20 m/s.

Relative speed in opposite direction = S₁ + S₂ = 400 ÷ 5 = 80 m/s.

Solving, S₁ = (80 + 20) ÷ 2 = 50 m/s and S₂ = (80 − 20) ÷ 2 = 30 m/s.

Speeds in km/h = 50 × (18/5) = 180 km/h and 30 × (18/5) = 108 km/h.

∴ The correct answer is 180 km/h and 108 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Length of first train (L₁) = 150 m

Length of second train (L₂) = 250 m

Time taken to cross in same direction (T₁) = 20 seconds

Time taken to cross in opposite direction (T₂) = 5 seconds

Formula Used:

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Total distance covered to cross each other = L₁ + L₂



Calculations:

⇒ Total Distance = 150 + 250 = 400 m

⇒ Let the speed of the first train be u m/s and the second train be v m/s.

⇒ When running in the same direction, relative speed = u − v

⇒ u − v = 400 ÷ 20 = 20 m/s ... (Equation 1)

⇒ When running in opposite directions, relative speed = u + v

⇒ u + v = 400 ÷ 5 = 80 m/s ... (Equation 2)

⇒ Adding Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ 2u = 100 ⇒ u = 50 m/s

⇒ Subtracting Equation 1 from Equation 2:

⇒ 2v = 60 ⇒ v = 30 m/s

⇒ Convert speeds to km/h by multiplying with (18/5):

⇒ Speed of first train = 50 × (18/5) = 180 km/h

⇒ Speed of second train = 30 × (18/5) = 108 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 180 km/h and 108 km/h.

Additional Information

Relative Speed

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). When moving in the same direction, it is the difference of their speeds (|S₁ − S₂|).

Distance While Crossing

When two trains cross each other, the total distance covered is always the sum of their lengths (L₁ + L₂), regardless of the direction they are moving.

Unit Conversion Trick

To rapidly convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply the value by 18/5. To convert from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18.

q: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 92 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and the policeman run at the speed of 90 km/h and 104.4 km/h, respectively. In how much time will the policeman catch the thief?
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Relative speed = 104.4 − 90 = 14.4 km/h

Relative speed in m/s = 14.4 × (5 / 18) = 4 m/s

Time to catch = Gap Distance ÷ Relative speed

Time = 92 ÷ 4 = 23 seconds

∴ The correct answer is 23 seconds.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial distance between policeman and thief = 92 m

Speed of policeman = 104.4 km/h

Speed of thief = 90 km/h



Formula Used:

Relative speed (running in the same direction) = Speed₁ − Speed₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Calculations:

⇒ Relative speed = 104.4 − 90 = 14.4 km/h

⇒ To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by (5 / 18)

⇒ Relative speed in m/s = 14.4 × (5 / 18) = 0.8 × 5 = 4 m/s

⇒ Time required to catch the thief = Distance ÷ Relative speed

⇒ Time = 92 ÷ 4

⇒ Time = 23 seconds

∴ The correct answer is 23 seconds.

Additional Information

Relative Speed

When two bodies are moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their speeds (S₁ − S₂). If moving in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (S₁ + S₂).

To convert a speed value from km/h into m/s, multiply the value by (5 / 18). Conversely, to convert from m/s into km/h, multiply by (18 / 5).

q: A motorboat, whose speed in 15 km/h in still water goes 50 km downstream and comes back in a total of 7 hours 30 minutes. The speed of the stream (in km/h) is:
solution:
Shortcut Trick

For equal distance upstream and downstream, Total Time = [Distance × (2 × Speed of Boat)] ÷ (Speed of Boat² − Stream Speed²)

⇒ 7.5 = [50 × (2 × 15)] ÷ (15² − s²)

⇒ 7.5 = 1500 ÷ (225 − s²)

⇒ 225 − s² = 200 ⇒ s² = 25

⇒ s = 5 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 5 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of the motorboat in still water (v) = 15 km/h

Distance covered in each direction (D) = 50 km

Total time taken (T) = 7 hours 30 minutes = 7.5 hours

Formula Used:

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Downstream Speed = v + s

Upstream Speed = v − s



Calculations:

Let the speed of the stream be s km/h.

⇒ Time taken downstream = 50 ÷ (15 + s)

⇒ Time taken upstream = 50 ÷ (15 − s)

Since the total time is 7.5 hours:

⇒ [50 ÷ (15 + s)] + [50 ÷ (15 − s)] = 7.5

Taking 50 common from the numerator:

⇒ 50 × [1 ÷ (15 + s) + 1 ÷ (15 − s)] = 7.5

⇒ 50 × [(15 − s + 15 + s) ÷ (15 + s)(15 − s)] = 7.5

⇒ 50 × [30 ÷ (225 − s²)] = 7.5

⇒ 1500 ÷ (225 − s²) = 7.5

⇒ 225 − s² = 1500 ÷ 7.5

⇒ 225 − s² = 200

⇒ s² = 225 − 200

⇒ s² = 25

⇒ s = 5 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 5 km/h.

Additional Information

Speed of Boat in Still Water

If the downstream speed is D and upstream speed is U, then the speed of the boat in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of Stream

If the downstream speed is D and upstream speed is U, then the speed of the stream = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Average Speed for Round Trip

When going downstream and returning upstream over the same distance, Average speed = (2 × D × U) ÷ (D + U).

q: A boat covers a distance of 55 km downstream in 5 hours while it takes 11 hours to cover the same distance upstream. What is the speed of the boat?
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Downstream Speed (D) = Distance ÷ Time = 55 ÷ 5 = 11 km/h

Upstream Speed (U) = Distance ÷ Time = 55 ÷ 11 = 5 km/h

Speed of boat in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2

⇒ (11 + 5) ÷ 2 = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 8 km/h.

Alternate Method



Given:

Distance covered = 55 km

Time taken downstream = 5 hours

Time taken upstream = 11 hours

Formula Used:

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Speed of Boat in Still Water = (Speed Downstream + Speed Upstream) ÷ 2

Calculations:

⇒ Downstream Speed = 55 ÷ 5 = 11 km/h

⇒ Upstream Speed = 55 ÷ 11 = 5 km/h

⇒ Speed of Boat in Still Water = (11 + 5) ÷ 2

⇒ Speed of Boat in Still Water = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 8 km/h.

Additional Information

Speed of the Stream

It is calculated as half the difference between downstream and upstream speeds: Vₛ = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Relationship Between Speeds

Downstream Speed (D) = Speed of Boat (Vb) + Speed of Stream (Vₛ).

Upstream Speed (U) = Speed of Boat (Vb) − Speed of Stream (Vₛ).

Average Speed for a Round Trip

If a boat goes a certain distance upstream and returns downstream to the original point, its average speed is given by (2 × D × U) ÷ (D + U).

q: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 100 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. If the speed of thief and policeman are 21 km/h and 23 km/h, respectively, then how far will the thief have to run before he is over taken?
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since the time of running is constant for both, the ratio of distances covered is equal to the ratio of their speeds.

Ratio of speeds (Police : Thief) = 23 : 21

Difference in distance ratio = 23 − 21 = 2 units, which is equal to the initial gap of 100 m.

⇒ 1 unit = 100 ÷ 2 = 50 m

⇒ Distance run by the thief = 21 units = 21 × 50 = 1050 m

∴ The correct answer is 1050 m.

Alternate Method



Given:

Distance between policeman and thief = 100 m

Speed of thief = 21 km/h

Speed of policeman = 23 km/h

Formula Used:

Relative Speed (same direction) = Speed₁ − Speed₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculations:

⇒ Relative speed = 23 − 21 = 2 km/h

⇒ Relative speed in m/s = 2 × (5 ÷ 18) = 5/9 m/s

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = 100 ÷ (5/9) = 180 seconds

⇒ Distance covered by the thief = Speed of thief × Time taken

⇒ Distance covered = [21 × (5 ÷ 18)] × 180

⇒ Distance covered = 21 × 50 = 1050 m

∴ The correct answer is 1050 m.

Additional Information

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗₐₜᵢvₑ = |S₁ − S₂|.

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two bodies move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗₐₜᵢvₑ = S₁ + S₂.

Proportionality of Distance and Speed

When the time traveled is constant, the distance covered is directly proportional to the speed: D₁/D₂ = S₁/S₂.

q: A policeman is chasing a thief at a speed of 82 km/h. The thief is 1300 m away and is running at a speed of 64 km/h. In how much time will the policeman catch the thief if both are riding on bikes?
solution:

Since both the policeman and the thief are moving in the same direction, relative speed = 82 − 64 = 18 km/h.

Convert relative speed to m/s = 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s.

Time required to cover 1300 m gap = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 1300 ÷ 5 = 260 sec.

∴ The correct answer is 260 sec.

Alternate Method

Speed of Policeman (S₁) = 82 km/h

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time taken = 1300 ÷ 5 = 260 seconds

∴ The correct answer is 260 sec.

Additional Information

Relative Speed

When two bodies are moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: SR = S₁ − S₂. When moving in opposite directions, it is the sum of their individual speeds: SR = S₁ + S₂.

Speed Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply the value by 18/5.

Average Speed

q: Two goods trains 132 m and 108 m in length are running towards each other on parallel tracks. The first train is running at a speed of 32 km/h and the second at a speed of 40 km/h. How much time will they take to cross each other after meeting?
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total distance = 132 + 108 = 240 m

Relative speed (opposite directions) = 32 + 40 = 72 km/h

Convert speed to m/s = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s

Time = Distance ÷ Speed = 240 ÷ 20 = 12 s

∴ The correct answer is 12 s.

Alternate Method



Given:

Length of first train (L₁) = 132 m

Length of second train (L₂) = 108 m

Speed of first train (V₁) = 32 km/h

Speed of second train (V₂) = 40 km/h

Formula Used:

Time taken to cross = Total distance ÷ Relative speed

For trains moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = V₁ + V₂

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/h × (5/18)

Calculations:

⇒ Total Distance = L₁ + L₂ = 132 + 108 = 240 m

⇒ Relative Speed = V₁ + V₂ = 32 + 40 = 72 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s

⇒ Time taken = 240 ÷ 20 = 12 s

∴ The correct answer is 12 s.

Additional Information

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: Vᵣₑₗ = |V₁ − V₂|.

Crossing a Stationary Object with Length

When a train crosses a bridge, tunnel, or platform, the total distance covered is the sum of the train's length and the object's length: Total Distance = Lₜᵣₐᵢₙ + Lₒbjₑ꜀ₜ.

Crossing a Stationary Point Object

When a train crosses a pole or a standing man, the distance covered is exactly equal to the length of the train: Total Distance = Lₜᵣₐᵢₙ.

Speed Unit Conversion Rule

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by (5/18). To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by (18/5).

q: Seema walks around a circular field at the rate of 3 rounds per hour, while Priya runs around it at the rate of 8 rounds per hour. They start in the same direction from the same point at 11:54 PM. They shall first cross each other at:
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Relative speed in the same direction = 8 − 3 = 5 rounds per hour.

This means Priya gains 5 complete rounds over Seema in 60 minutes.

They will cross each other when Priya gains exactly 1 complete round.

Time to gain 1 round = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 minutes.

Crossing time = 11:54 p.m. + 12 minutes = 12:06 a.m.

∴ The correct answer is 12:06 a.m.

Alternate Method



Given:

⇒ Speed of Seema = 3 rounds/hr

⇒ Speed of Priya = 8 rounds/hr

⇒ Starting time = 11:54 p.m.

Formula Used:

⇒ Relative Speed (same direction) = Speed₁ − Speed₂

⇒ Time to cross for the first time = 1 round distance ÷ Relative Speed

Calculations:

⇒ Since they are moving in the same direction, relative speed = 8 − 3 = 5 rounds/hr

⇒ They cross each other when the faster person (Priya) covers exactly 1 more round than the slower person (Seema).

⇒ Time taken to gain 1 round = 1 ÷ 5 hours

⇒ Time taken in minutes = (1/5) × 60 = 12 minutes

⇒ Crossing time = 11:54 p.m. + 12 minutes

⇒ 11:54 p.m. + 6 minutes = 12:00 a.m. (Midnight)

⇒ 12:00 a.m. + 6 minutes = 12:06 a.m.

∴ The correct answer is 12:06 a.m.

Additional Information

Circular Motion (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction on a circular track, the time taken to meet for the first time anywhere on the track is calculated as Track Length ÷ (Speed₁ − Speed₂).

Circular Motion (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies move in opposite directions, their relative speed increases. The time taken to meet for the first time is Track Length ÷ (Speed₁ + Speed₂).

Meeting at the Starting Point

The time taken for both runners to meet exactly at the starting point is the LCM (Least Common Multiple) of the individual times taken by each to complete one full round.

Number of Distinct Meeting Points

If the ratio of their speeds is a:b (in simplest form), they will meet at exactly (a − b) distinct points if running in the same direction, and at (a + b) distinct points if running in opposite directions.

q: Suppose P starts walking at a speed of 8 km/h. After 8 hours B started travelling on a bicycle at a speed of 24 km/h. The distance from the starting B can catch P is:
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Head start distance covered by P in 8 hours = 8 × 8 = 64 km.

Relative speed of B (moving in the same direction) = 24 − 8 = 16 km/h.

Time taken by B to catch P = 64 ÷ 16 = 4 hours.

Distance from the starting point = B's speed × time = 24 × 4 = 96 km.

∴ The correct answer is 96 km.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of P = 8 km/h

Speed of B = 24 km/h

Head start time for P = 8 hours



Formula Used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative Speed (same direction) = Speed of B − Speed of P

Catch-up Time = Initial Gap Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Calculations:

⇒ Distance covered by P before B starts = 8 × 8 = 64 km

⇒ This 64 km is the gap that B needs to cover to catch P.

⇒ Relative speed of B to P = 24 − 8 = 16 km/h

⇒ Time taken by B to close the gap = 64 ÷ 16 = 4 hours

⇒ Distance from the starting point = B's speed × Time taken

⇒ Distance = 24 × 4 = 96 km

∴ The correct answer is 96 km.

Additional Information

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects travel in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂.

Catch-up Time Formula

The time required to overtake or catch a head-start object is given by: Time = Initial Gap Distance ÷ Relative Speed.

Distance by Ratio Method

When the travel time is constant for two moving bodies, the ratio of the distances they cover is directly proportional to the ratio of their speeds: D₁/D₂ = S₁/S₂.

q: A policeman noticed a thief at some distance. The policeman started running to catch the thief and the thief also started running at the same time. The speed of both policeman and the thief was 12 km per hour and 10 km per hour, respectively. It took 30 minutes for the policeman to catch the thief. Find the initial distance (in metres) between them.
solution:
Shortcut Trick

When running in the same direction, Relative Speed = SP − ST.

Relative speed = 12 − 10 = 2 km/h

Time = 30 minutes = 1/2 hour

Initial distance = Relative speed × Time = 2 × 1/2 = 1 km

Convert to metres: 1 km = 1000 m

∴ The correct answer is 1000 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of policeman (SP) = 12 km/h

Speed of thief (ST) = 10 km/h

Time taken to catch the thief (t) = 30 minutes = 30 ÷ 60 = 0.5 hours

Distance = Speed × Time



Calculation:

⇒ The policeman and the thief run in the same direction, so we calculate their relative speed.

⇒ Relative speed = 12 − 10 = 2 km/h

⇒ Initial Distance = Relative Speed × Time taken to catch

⇒ Initial Distance = 2 km/h × 0.5 hours

⇒ Initial Distance = 1 km

⇒ Convert kilometers to meters: 1 km = 1000 m

∴ The correct answer is 1000 m.

Additional Information

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. When they move in opposite directions towards each other, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversions for Speed and Distance

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert m/s back to km/h, multiply by 18/5. Always ensure units match before applying distance formulas.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If equal distances are covered at speeds S₁ and S₂, then Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

q: Two athletes are participating in a race on a circular track of 220 m. Ravi runs at the speed of 22 m/s, while Kapil runs at the speed of 11 m/s. They start from the same point, at the same time and in the same direction. After how many seconds will they meet for the first time?
solution:
Shortcut Trick

When running in the same direction on a circular track, the relative speed is the difference of their speeds.

Relative Speed = 22 − 11 = 11 m/s

Time to meet = Track Length ÷ Relative Speed

Time = 220 ÷ 11 = 20 seconds

∴ The correct answer is 20 seconds.

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time taken = 220 ÷ 11

Additional Information

Meeting at the Starting Point

The time taken to meet exactly at the starting point for the first time is the LCM of the individual times taken by each runner to complete one full round.

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two bodies move in opposite directions around a track, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Number of Distinct Meeting Points

When running in the same direction, the total number of distinct meeting points on the circular track is the difference of their speeds when expressed in their simplest ratio.

q: In a circular race of 1600 m in length, Bhaskar and Vinay start with speeds of 27 km/h and 45 km/h starting at the same time from the same point. When will they meet for the first time on the track when running in the opposite directions and the same direction, respectively?
solution:

q: A thief takes off on his bike at a certain speed, after seeing a police car at a distance of 250 m. The police car starts chasing the thief and catches him. If the thief runs 1.5 km before being caught and the speed of the police car is 70 km/h, then what is the speed of thief's bike (in km/h)?

q: P and Q take part in 400 m race. P runs at 12 km/hr. P gives Q a start of 20 m and still beats him by 13 seconds. The speed of Q is: (Round up to two decimal places.)
